Start working on Linear ticket eng-1884. See parent issue for details. by fetching its details and creating a dedicated git worktree.

## Steps

### 1. Validate input
- `eng-1884. See parent issue for details.` should be a Linear ticket ID like `ENG-1271`. If missing or malformed, ask the user.

### 2. Fetch ticket details from Linear
- Use `mcp__linear-server__get_issue` with the issue ID `eng-1884. See parent issue for details.`
- Extract: title, description, and `branchName` (Linear provides this)
- If the Linear tool is unavailable, ask the user for a branch name manually

### 3. Determine branch name
- Use the `branchName` field from Linear if available (it's already formatted correctly)
- Otherwise derive it: lowercase the ticket ID + hyphenated slug of the title
  - Example: `ENG-1271 Implement filter search` → `eng-1271-implement-filter-search`
  - Strip special characters, replace spaces with hyphens, truncate to ~60 chars

### 4. Create git worktree
Run these from the repo root (the main working directory, not an existing worktree):

```bash
# Fetch latest main so the worktree starts from up-to-date origin/main
git fetch origin main

# Check if branch already exists
git branch --list <branch-name>

# Check if worktree already exists
git worktree list | grep <branch-name>
```

- **If worktree already exists**: skip to step 5, just `cd` into `.claude/worktrees/<branch-name>`
- **If branch does NOT exist**: `git worktree add -b <branch-name> .claude/worktrees/<branch-name> origin/main`
- **If branch already exists but no worktree**: reset the branch to `origin/main` first, then add the worktree:
  ```bash
  git branch -f <branch-name> origin/main
  git worktree add .claude/worktrees/<branch-name> <branch-name>
  ```

### 5. Enter the worktree
**Do NOT use the `EnterWorktree` tool** — it always creates a brand-new worktree and will duplicate the one you just created.

Instead, use `cd` to switch into the worktree directory:
```bash
cd .claude/worktrees/<branch-name>
```

All subsequent commands should run from this path.

### 6. Install dependencies and set up the worktree
After entering the worktree, run the following to bootstrap the environment:

```bash
pnpm install
```

This is required because worktrees share git objects but each needs its own `node_modules`.

### 6b. Copy .env files from the main repo into the worktree
`.env` files are gitignored, so each worktree needs its own copies. After `pnpm install`, copy all `.env` files (excluding `.env.example` files) from the main repo root into the matching relative paths in the worktree.

The main repo root is the working directory you were in before entering the worktree (e.g. `/Users/trang.doan/Desktop/code/discourse-graph`).

Run:
```bash
# From the main repo root, find all .env files (not .env.example) and copy them into the worktree
find . -name ".env*" \
  -not -name ".env.example" \
  -not -path "./.git/*" \
  -not -path "./node_modules/*" \
  -not -path "./.claude/worktrees/*" \
  | while read f; do
      dest=".claude/worktrees/<branch-name>/$f"
      mkdir -p "$(dirname "$dest")"
      cp "$f" "$dest"
    done
```

Report which files were copied so the user can confirm.

### 7. Ask the user which app to start
Ask the user which app they want to run in dev mode. Common options:
- **Roam**: `SUPABASE_USE_DB=none pnpm -C <worktree>/apps/roam dev`
- **Obsidian**: `SUPABASE_USE_DB=local pnpm -C <worktree>/apps/obsidian dev`
- **None**: just set up the environment without starting a dev server

If the user says Roam, also switch the Roam dev symlink:
```bash
ln -sfn <worktree>/apps/roam/dist ~/roam-ext-dev
```
and remind them to reload the developer extension in Roam.

Run the chosen dev command in the background so the user can continue working.

**Dev server gotchas** (learned the hard way — don't rediscover these):

- The filter flag is `--filter`, not `--F`. Turbo 2.5.6 rejects `--F=roam` outright.
- Prefer `pnpm -C <abs-path> <app> dev` over `turbo dev --filter=<app>`. `turbo dev --filter=roam`
  also runs the `@repo/database#dev` dependency, which requires Docker Desktop plus an explicit
  `SUPABASE_USE_DB`; if Docker isn't running turbo fails the *entire* run even though the app
  itself built fine. Going through `pnpm -C` skips the dependency graph.
- `SUPABASE_USE_DB` must be one of `local | branch | production | none | implicit`
  (see `packages/database/src/dbDotEnv.mjs`). Use `none` for work that doesn't touch the database.
- **Always bake the absolute worktree path into the command.** The Bash tool's cwd resets to the
  main repo between calls, so a backgrounded `pnpm --filter roam dev` with no path silently builds
  the *main repo's* `dist` — not the worktree the symlink points at. `pnpm -C <abs-path>` makes the
  path intrinsic to the command so it can't be dropped.
- After starting, verify before reporting success: confirm the log says `built with 0 errors` **and**
  that `<worktree>/apps/roam/dist` has a fresh mtime. A background task that failed still returns a
  task ID.

### 8. Ingest any saved session context
The branch may have been worked on before (e.g. reset from an existing branch).
Check for recorded session context:

```ts
    const src = await uploadImageShapeToRoam({ editor, shape: shape as TLImageShape });
```

Target selection uses reactive `useValue`, hover *or* sole selection, and skips locked shapes:

```ts
const isConvertibleImage = (shape?: TLShape | null): shape is TLImageShape =>
  shape?.type === "image" && !shape.isLocked;

const imageShape = useValue<TLImageShape | null>("imageConvertTarget", () => {
  if (!editor.isIn("select.idle")) return null;
  const hovered = editor.getHoveredShape();
  if (isConvertibleImage(hovered)) return hovered;
  const selected = editor.getOnlySelectedShape();
  return isConvertibleImage(selected) ? selected : null;
```

```ts
const bounds = editor.getShapePageBounds(imageShape.id);
const vp = editor.pageToViewport({ x: bounds.minX, y: bounds.minY });
return { left: vp.x + BUTTON_INSET, top: vp.y + BUTTON_INSET };  // BUTTON_INSET = 8
```

```ts
onSuccess: async ({ text, uid, nodeType }) => {
```

```tsx
export const CustomContextMenu = ({ extensionAPI, allNodes }: {...}) => {
  const editor = useEditor();
  const selectedShape = useValue("selectedShape", () => editor.getOnlySelectedShape(), [editor]);
  const selectedShapes = useValue("selectedShapes", () => editor.getSelectedShapes(), [editor]);
  const shareableResults = getShareableCanvasSelectionResults({ shapes: selectedShapes });
  const isTextSelected = selectedShape?.type === "text";
  const isImageSelected = selectedShape?.type === "image";
  const arrowRelationOptions = useValue("arrowRelationOptions", () => {
      if (!selectedShape || selectedShape.type !== "arrow") return null;
      const boundNodes = getArrowBoundNodeInfo(editor, selectedShape);
      if (!boundNodes) return null;
      const relationTypes = getValidRelationTypesBetween(editor, boundNodes.startId, boundNodes.endId);
      if (relationTypes.length === 0) return null;
      return { arrowId: selectedShape.id, ...boundNodes, relationTypes };
    }, [editor, selectedShape]);

  return (
    <DefaultContextMenu>
      <DefaultContextMenuContent />
      {shareableResults.length > 0 && (
        <TldrawUiMenuGroup id="share-data-group">
          <TldrawUiMenuItem id="share-data" label="Share Data" readonlyOk onSelect={() => { … renderShareDataDialog(…) }} />

          </TldrawUiMenuSubmenu>
        </TldrawUiMenuGroup>

      {arrowRelationOptions && (
        <TldrawUiMenuGroup id="relation-group">
          <TldrawUiMenuSubmenu id="relation-submenu" label="Relation">
            {arrowRelationOptions.relationTypes.map((rt) => (
              <TldrawUiMenuItem key={rt.id} id={`relation-${rt.id}`} label={rt.label}
                onSelect={async () => {
                  const arrow = editor.getShape<TLArrowShape>(arrowRelationOptions.arrowId);
```

## Context

Parent request **FEE-824** (Joel Chan): *"convert tldraw shape to discourse node (if it has text in it)"*. Neither ticket has a written description — the titles are the whole spec.

Everything else — including the sticky notes and labelled rectangles users actually draw on — falls through to a silent no-op.

So this is a **widening of an existing feature**, not a new one. The gate is the deliverable.

tldraw here is **2.4.6** (v2), where `geo` and `note` shapes carry `props.text` as a plain string — no `richText` migration needed. (`apps/obsidian` is on 3.14.2; do not copy patterns across.)

Decisions taken with the user:
- **Scope**: add `geo` + `note`. Not arrows (they already convert to *relations* via a sibling menu entry — overloading them would confuse the two), not frames (they carry `name`, not `text`).
- **Selection**: single-shape only, unchanged.
- **Base**: stack on `eng-1356` (PR #1427, open), which already extracted the conversion logic into a reusable helper.

## Step 0 — Rebase onto eng-1356

The worktree is currently on `origin/main`. Rebase it onto the ENG-1356 branch so the extracted helper is available and `uiOverrides.tsx` doesn't conflict:

```bash

```

This PR then targets that branch, not `main`, and cannot merge until #1427 does.

## Approach

Today the shape-type test is duplicated in three places and expressed as two booleans:

- `uiOverrides.tsx:410-411,457,462` — `isTextSelected` / `isImageSelected` gate the submenu, and `isImageSelected` separately filters out `page-node`

Adding two more shape types to that shape would mean four call sites drifting apart. Instead, **replace the booleans with one text-extraction function** and let every site derive its behaviour from the result.

### 1. `apps/roam/src/components/canvas/convertShapeToDiscourseNode.ts`

```ts

// per FEE-824 ("if it has text in it").
export const getConvertibleShapeText = (
  shape?: TLShape | null,
): string | null => {
  if (!shape || shape.isLocked) return null;
  if (shape.type === "image") return "";
  if (!TEXT_SHAPE_TYPES.includes(shape.type)) return null;
  const text = (shape.props as { text?: string }).text?.trim() ?? "";
  if (shape.type !== "text" && !text) return null;
  return text;
};
```

`null` = not convertible; a string = convertible, and that string is the dialog's initial text.

- `text` shapes stay convertible when empty (they are already, and an empty text shape is a degenerate case users don't hit).
- `geo`/`note` require non-empty text — this is FEE-824's stated condition, and it keeps "Convert To" out of the menu for every plain rectangle on the board.

### 2. `apps/roam/src/components/canvas/uiOverrides.tsx`

- Replace `isTextSelected`/`isImageSelected` with:
  ```ts
  const convertibleText = getConvertibleShapeText(selectedShape);
  const isImageSelected = selectedShape?.type === "image";
  ```
  Keep `isImageSelected` — it is still needed for the `page-node` filter (line 462), which is about images not supporting a key-image flag, not about the gate.
- Gate becomes `{convertibleText !== null && ( … )}`.
- In `getOnSelectForShape`, collapse the `text` branch into a text-shape-agnostic one:
  ```ts
  const text = getConvertibleShapeText(shape);
  if (text === null) return () => {};
  if (shape.type === "image") { /* unchanged upload branch */ }
  return () => openDialogAndCreateShape({ initialText: text });
  ```

### 3. `apps/roam/src/components/canvas/ConvertToDialog.tsx`

Same gate, so the `?C` path and the right-click path can't diverge:

```ts

const convertibleText = oneShapeSelected
  ? getConvertibleShapeText(selectedShapes[0])
  : null;

```

Keep the local `isImageSelected` for the `page-node` filter.

- `replaceShapeWithDiscourseNode` (`convertShapeToDiscourseNode.ts`) — already typed `TLShape` and only reads `shape.x/y/id`, so it handles geo/note with no modification.
- `renderModifyNodeDialog` (`ModifyNodeDialog.tsx`) — node title entry, template application, `createDiscourseNode`.
- `calcCanvasNodeSizeAndImg`, `DISCOURSE_NODE_SHAPE_TYPE`.

`replaceShapeWithDiscourseNode` deletes the source shape and creates a new one, so **arrows bound to a converted shape will unbind and dangle**. Out of scope here; worth a follow-up ticket if verification shows it's ugly.

| `apps/roam/src/components/canvas/uiOverrides.tsx` | gate + `getOnSelectForShape` use the helper |
| `apps/roam/src/components/canvas/ConvertToDialog.tsx` | same gate + error copy |

Roughly 40 lines net. No new dependencies, no schema/migration changes, no shape-util changes.

## Verification

Per `CLAUDE.local.md`, no unit tests for Roam UI work — verification is typecheck, lint, build, and the running app.

1. `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile && pnpm ci:validate` from the repo root.
2. Dev server is already running against this worktree and `~/roam-ext-dev` points here; reload the developer extension in Roam and open a canvas page.
3. Manual passes, right-click each:
   - **Sticky note with text** → "Convert To" present → pick a node type → dialog opens prefilled with the note's text → confirm → note is replaced by a discourse node shape at the same position, and the Roam page exists with the node's template applied.
   - **Rectangle with text** → same.

   - **Arrow** → still offers "Relation", not "Convert To".
   - **Two shapes selected** → no "Convert To" (single-selection gate intact).

```ts
// per FEE-824 ("if it has text in it").
export const getConvertibleShapeText = (
  shape?: TLShape | null,
): string | null => {
  if (!shape || shape.isLocked) return null;
  if (shape.type === "image") return "";
  if (!TEXT_SHAPE_TYPES.includes(shape.type)) return null;
```

## Phase 1 — Trim the comments

Only comments **you added on this branch**. Never rewrite comments that belong to
committed work — it inflates the diff with churn a reviewer has to read past.

```bash
git diff --stat "$BASE"...HEAD
git diff "$BASE"...HEAD | grep -nE '^\+\s*(//|/\*|\*|\{/\*)'
```

**Every surviving comment is one line.** Multi-line blocks and JSDoc paragraphs get
compressed, not preserved.

**Keep** a comment only when it says something the code cannot:

- A platform or build quirk with a non-obvious cause — a host CSS rule that outranks
  a utility class, a missing preflight, a library default that bites.
- A deliberate choice a reader would otherwise "fix": an uncontrolled input, a
  suppressed default, a two-step interaction, a guard that looks redundant.
- Why an obvious simpler approach does *not* work.
- A layout or structural decision that is easy to tidy up and thereby break.
- A cross-file invariant that is invisible from this file alone.

**Delete** a comment when it:

- Restates the line below it, or narrates what a well-named function already says.
- Defends a choice nobody would reverse (the ordinary, expected implementation).
- Documents code that no longer exists after a rewrite.
- Is a section banner or a decorative divider.

Ambiguity test: *if I deleted this, would a competent reviewer make a wrong change?*
No → delete it.

## Phase 2 — Self-review the diff

Read the repo's own rules first and check the diff against them, because these are
exactly the comments a reviewer or bot will leave:

```bash
cat AGENTS.md CLAUDE.md STYLE_GUIDE.md 2>/dev/null
find . -name AGENTS.md -not -path '*/node_modules/*'   # per-app rules override the root
```

Fix anything the diff violates. Common catches:

- Inline `style={{...}}` for a static value where a utility class works. Computed
  values (per-item colours) legitimately stay inline.
- Hand-rolled CSS where the platform exposes a variable or an existing class.
- `type` vs `interface`; missing explicit return types; `any`.
- Function declarations where the codebase uses arrow functions.
- Positional-index assumptions across two lists that can differ.
- Console logging in apps that require a user-facing notice instead.
- New dependencies where the platform already ships an equivalent.

Then the checks the CI will run, and the project's own verification story:

```bash
pnpm check-types && pnpm lint      # in the changed app
npx prettier --check <changed files>
```

If the change is observable at runtime, exercise it and say so in the body with
concrete numbers. A body that claims "verified" without saying how is worth less
than one that names what was measured.

## Phase 3 — Write the body and open it

**Every word you write here follows `dg-engineering-writing-style`** — the body, the
title, the inline PR comments, the reply to a reviewer. Read
`<repo-root>/.agents/skills/dg-engineering-writing-style/SKILL.md` before drafting.
What it changes in practice:

- No em dashes as sentence punctuation. Use a period, comma, colon, or parentheses.
- One term per concept, all the way through. Do not alternate "node type" and "schema"

- Replace "handle", "support", "improve", "update" with the behavior: "reads the format

<skill-prompt>
Run a pre-PR review of the current change set. This is NOT a checklist to ponder — it is a sequence of verification steps with pass/fail outcomes. You must actually run the greps/traces; "I believe this is fine" without having looked is a failed step. Built from an autopsy of 97 real reviewer comments (2026-03→07) — 46 violated rules a previous skill already "had" but never enforced; recall is not verification — and refreshed 2026-08-28 against the 2026-07→08 corpus (~200 human review comments across sid's and teammates' PRs).

- `engineering-context.md` — team philosophies and hard-learned lessons (the *why* behind every check below)
- `db-domain-invariants.md` — current schema/data-layer facts (the data-layer pass checks the diff against every entry)

## Step 0 — Inventory

The change set is the FULL PR diff: `git diff <base>...HEAD` (merge-base three-dot against the PR's base branch — the stack parent for stacked PRs, else main) plus staged/unstaged changes. Never review only the latest commits: reviewers see the whole PR, and code that landed on the branch before this run is still your surface. Classify changed files:
- **DATA**: `packages/database/**`, `*.sql`, any file containing a Supabase/PostgREST call (`.from(`), datalog query, or cross-app contract type
- **FRONTEND**: `apps/roam/**`, `apps/obsidian/**`, `apps/website/**` UI code
- **OTHER**: tests, docs, config

Steps 2 and 3 are scoped: skip the data-layer pass if no DATA files changed; skip the frontend pass if no FRONTEND files changed. Never skip steps 1 and 4.

## Step 1 — Mechanical sweeps (always run; each is an action, not a question)

1a. **Reuse gate.** List every NEW named thing in the diff (function, type, component, constant, enum, marker string). For each, run a grep across `apps/roam/src/utils`, `packages/utils`, `packages/database/src`, and sibling files for the core operation or shape. Report what you searched and what you found. A new thing duplicating an existing one is a finding. Special case: every inline string-literal union (`"X" | "Y"`) gets its members grepped in `packages/database/src/dbTypes.ts`; members matching a generated enum → must use `Enums<"…">`.

1b. **Justification sweep.** For every added default value, optional prop/field, state variable, fallback (`?? x`, `|| x`), and kept-through-refactor line: name the concrete code path that exercises it. Trace return types through call sites — if a function always returns `T`, a `?? fallback` at its call site is dead code; say so. No path → finding: delete it.

1c. **Literal hoist.** Repeated or typo-prone string literals (prop keys, selectors, attribute names, ids) appearing more than once or shared with other files → must be a named constant defined once.

1d. **Type honesty.** For every `as`, `any`, `unknown`, `!` (non-null assertion), `?.`, `void`, and `|| default` in the diff: can the value actually be null/absent there? Verify against the type at its source, don't guess. Assertion where a guard or upstream fix is possible → finding. A `!` that must survive gets an inline comment saying why it's safe — mdroidian flags every bare `!` (#1329, #1324).

1e. **Explainability.** For each hunk: one sentence, why is this here in service of the ticket? Reorderings, reformats, removals, and leftover scaffolding you can't explain → finding: revert.

1f. **Call-graph pass (review the resulting system, not the diff).** For every exported symbol added or modified, and every function parameter added: grep ALL call sites across `apps/` and `packages/` and read them. Findings:
- a parameter that only one caller supplies (or that every caller could omit) → internalize or remove it
- a wrapper that after this change only renames/forwards or adds one trivial field → collapse it into its caller
- an export with zero external consumers → unexport
- an existing caller whose behavior silently changes (check what it did with the old return shape — e.g. did it append `Z` to a timestamp you now normalize?)
Reviewers read the post-state code, not the diff; a hunk that looks justified in isolation can leave the system with dead indirection.

1g. **Comment audit.** List every comment line ADDED by the diff. Delete any that restates the code or narrates the change — "Claude, chill on the comments" is a real review quote, left twice (#1222, #1321), and "some unnecessary comments here" a third time (#1292). A comment referencing context not present in the file (another PR, a discussion, another platform's behavior) either becomes self-contained or dies: reviewers reply "What is F12?" / "What is the same reason?" to comments they can't parse cold (#1315, #1292, #1284). Keep only comments stating a constraint the code can't show.

1h. **Second-lookup check.** For every new fetch, map-build, `.find`, or helper lookup: trace where its input data was constructed — was the looked-up value already present there (on the row, the batch, an upstream type)? If yes → thread the field through the pipeline types instead of re-deriving downstream. (#1266: importer re-fetched `schema_id` that `SharedNode` already carried; #1317: `getFormatByNodeTypeUid()` second lookup when `matchingNodeType.format` was in hand at the construction site.)

1i. **Workflow injection (only if `.github/workflows/` changed).** Any `${{ inputs.* }}` / `${{ github.event.* }}` interpolated directly into a `run:` script is shell injection — pass it through `env:` and use a quoted variable, validated against a fully anchored pattern (#1253).

## Step 2 — Data-layer pass (only if DATA files changed)

2a. Open `db-domain-invariants.md` and check the diff against EVERY entry. For each entry state: applies / doesn't apply / VIOLATION. Do not summarize the file — walk it.

2b. **Provenance trace.** For every value read from a PostgREST response or datalog result used in the diff: name the source column, grep its type in `packages/database/supabase/schemas/*.sql`, then judge the code handling it (timestamps are the known killer — naive UTC, no `Z`).

2c. **Query review.** For every `.from(...)` chain (new or modified): required domain filters present (arity, is_schema, variant)? Any client-side `.filter`/`.find`/sort the request could express? Payload columns in a listing path? Paginated with a unique total order? Inside a loop that should be batched?

2d. **Contract check.** New/changed shared types: required-vs-optional modeled from real cases (does every producer actually supply it)? Identity carried once (RID) not duplicated decomposed? Consistent with `crossAppContracts.ts` and with what the Obsidian side already assumes — check its consumer code, don't assume.

2e. **Converter matrix.** A field added or renamed on a cross-app contract or schema type must be handled in EVERY converter, BOTH directions, or explicitly deferred with a ticket named in the PR. Enumerate the cells and mark each handled/deferred: `packages/database/src/lib/crossAppConverters.ts` (CrossApp→db), `packages/database/src/lib/dbToCrossAppConverters.ts` (db→CrossApp), `apps/roam/src/utils/roamToCrossAppConverters.ts`, and Obsidian's parse/produce paths (`importNodes.ts` parsers, publish side). maparent asked for the missing direction on #1316 AND #1317: "This PR is adding a field; it should handle that field in both translation directions."

2f. **Flag-gated writes.** For every new DB write path: which user-visible flag or action authorizes it? Sync flag off ⇒ the user expects NO DB communication; a silent maintenance write (backfill, migration) needs explicit call-out in the PR, and its outcome reports to PostHog — never a user toast (#1332).

## Step 3 — Frontend pass (only if FRONTEND files changed)

Check against the frontend lessons in `engineering-context.md`, mechanically:
- grep the diff for `style=`, `class-[`/`-[` arbitrary values, hex colors → Tailwind-scale violations
- grep for `window.roamAlphaAPI` legacy paths (sync `.q`, `async.backend`) → current-API violations
- settings writes → must go through block-props accessors, preserving the store gate
- new UI elements → which flag gates them (including EXISTING flags the new surface must respect, e.g. `autoCanvasRelations` on #1272); user-facing failures → PostHog + toast, not `console.error`
- names: every new variable/setter/label states exactly what it holds or does; UI labels reuse existing product vocabulary ("discourse context", not an invented synonym — #1255)
- grep the diff for positional child access on settings/config trees (`tree[3]`, `.children[0]`) → look up by key with `getSubTree`; position compiles today and silently writes to the wrong parent after any reorder (#1302)
- persisted/saved data stores stable IDs (shape id, uid), never display names — names are UI-only and subject to change (#1222: save `frameShapeId`, not `frameName`)
- `Page`, `Block`, and `Any` are reserved built-in vocabulary: excluded from user-selectable type lists (#1298), never name-resolved to/from a remote schema, never creatable as configured types (#1331 was blocked on exactly this; #1272 applied the same rule on canvas)
- a panel that replaces or extends existing UI matches it pixel-wise — proportions, selected-tab highlight, centering; reviewers screenshot-compare against the original (#1255, #1272). Empty states key on the right condition (no relation *instances* ≠ no relation *types*, #1255)
- user-facing strings use user vocabulary — a toast saying "backfilled" is a finding; internal bookkeeping reports to PostHog only (#1332)

## Step 4 — Process gate

- Every hunk maps to this PR's ticket; unrelated changes → revert or explicitly annotate. Out-of-scope improvements a reviewer might request → pre-empt by naming them in the PR with a Linear ticket ("X is deferred to ENG-YYYY").
- **One problem, ~<500 lines.** A PR solves a single problem in under ~500 changed lines before tests (mdroidian's stated bar, #1222). Real drive-by bug fixes split into their own ticket — and get fixed at their source layer (a roamjs-components bug is fixed in roamjs-components, not patched locally).
- **Bot-comment gate.** Before requesting human review: every codex/graphite/devin comment is either fixed or answered with why-not, and resolved. mdroidian's first pass is frequently just "See codex comments" / "address the bot reviews … and click resolve" (#1257, #1309, #1320) — an unresolved bot thread costs a full review round-trip.
- **Chain coverage.** For a PR in a stacked or sibling-ticket chain: does the union of this PR + named sibling tickets cover both platforms and both data directions? "This only handles Obsidian-origin — where's Roam-origin?" is maparent's most repeated 07–08 comment (#1267, #1269, #1316). Name the gap and the ticket that owns it in the PR before he does.
- **Guard removals are argued in the PR.** Removing an existence check or gate: state the cases it protected and why each is now safe (idempotent re-upsert, upstream guarantee). #1280's check removal survived review, but through a 3-comment thread that one PR annotation would have preempted.
- **Refactor/extraction parity table.** If this PR moves or extracts code (util → shared package, file split, API swap): produce a table of old symbol → new symbol → `identical` or `changed: <why>`. Every not-1:1 replacement is a decision the reviewer WILL ask about ("could you walk through those decisions?") — enumerate them before they do. The table goes in the PR description.
- Runtime proof: does this change have a surface a unit test can't exercise (UI, load-order, multi-user)? If yes, a demo is REQUIRED, not noted (`/demo-handoff`). If the diff touches DOM observers, drag/hover interactions, or rendered Roam surfaces: emit a **regression matrix** — surfaces (main window, right sidebar, left sidebar, Kanban, query-builder link/embed/render views, canvas) × content shapes (single-line, multiline/wrapping, nested references, page titles) — marking which cells this change can affect; the demo must drive every affected cell, with the mouse cursor visible in the recording, and any bug you claim fixed must be re-driven by you after the fix. Video quality bar (#1298): signal each state change visually (a quick caption/toast — "before fix" / "on branch"), don't carry it in narration alone, and cut narration that states the obvious ("every relation has a source and destination" earned a 🙄 from mdroidian).
- Reviewer context: list the bullets the PR description must contain (what was removed and why, temporary code, decisions made, deferrals + tickets). Test: could someone review this without asking a question?
- **Inherited decisions carry breadcrumbs.** Any code that exists because of a review decision on a PREVIOUS PR (a reviewer's direction, a contract agreed in another thread) gets a draft line-comment citing that source ("per maparent on #1214: local IDs may already be RIDs"). Without the breadcrumb the next reviewer re-litigates it.

## Output

1. **Findings**, ranked by severity, each: file:line — what — why it matters (cite the context-doc entry or the verification step that failed) — concrete fix.
2. **Verification log** — one line per mechanical step: what you ran/checked and the outcome. This proves the steps happened; a review with findings but no log is invalid.
2b. **Draft PR annotations** — ready-to-post, line-anchored comments explaining every non-obvious decision (guidepost style: what this block does and why, inherited-decision citations, parity-table deltas). Proven repeatedly: #1214, and in 07–08 reviewers replied to annotations in-thread and accepted the argument (#1280 "I accept this argument. Approving.", #1331). Also annotate every LARGE removal or moved block ("this was refactored into abc.ts") — mdroidian asked for exactly this on #1320. Posting them is part of finishing the PR, not optional polish.
2c. All reviewer-facing prose this skill emits — PR description bullets, draft annotations, deferral notes, parity tables — follows the team writing style skill at `<repo-root>/.agents/skills/dg-engineering-writing-style/SKILL.md` (mdroidian's #1278): lead with the point, one term per concept, replace vague verbs ("handle", "support") with the specific behavior, no em dashes, shortest version that keeps the nuance.
3. **Predicted review** (simulation, not identity): given the reviewers' comment history — mdroidian: frontend craftsmanship, dead code, reuse, naming, comment noise, bare `!`, second lookups, design parity with existing UI, reserved vocabulary (Page/Block/Any), unresolved bot comments, demo-video quality, Socratic "why is this here?"; maparent: schema/contract correctness, query shape, the missing converter direction, chain/sibling-ticket coverage gaps ("this only handles Obsidian-origin"), values re-fetched that the pipeline already carries, partial-failure semantics, Obsidian-parity of UX decisions, "worth calling out in another task?", "what does the data look like in 6 months?" — list the comments each would most likely leave on the remaining diff. These are forecasts to fix or preempt in the PR description, not instructions to please anyone.
4. If a pass is clean, say so explicitly. Do not manufacture findings; ~11% of historical review comments were not catchable pre-PR (product/1:1 context) — surface open questions instead of contorting.

Anti-weasel rules: no "not harmful, just unnecessary" (unnecessary = delete), no "acceptable for consistency" (a no-op kept for symmetry is cargo-culting), no noting facts without stating the conclusion they imply. If you have the information that leads to a finding, state the finding.

# Engineering Context — discourse-graph

What you need to know to do good work in this codebase: how the team thinks, and the lessons we paid for. This is context for doing the task well — not a reviewer to please. Every entry carries its *why*; if the why doesn't apply to your situation, reasoning from first principles beats rule-following.

Companion file: `db-domain-invariants.md` (same directory) — greppable schema/data-layer facts. Read it before touching `packages/database`, any Supabase query, or cross-app contract code.

---

## Working philosophies

**Every line is a liability — justify it or delete it.** The most common review comment on our PRs, by far, is a variant of "why is this here?" (defaults nobody hits, props kept through refactors, state vars with one writer and no reader, `?? fallback` on a value that can't be null). The bar: for each line, name the real code path that needs it. "It doesn't hurt" is not a justification; unused code misleads the next reader about what can happen.

**Reuse before writing — and actually search, don't recall.** The single largest class of review feedback (16+ comments in 4 months) is "we already have this": utils, shared components, generated types, markers, constants. Memory of the codebase is unreliable; a 10-second grep is not. Before writing any new function/type/component/constant: grep `apps/roam/src/utils`, `packages/utils`, `packages/database/src/dbTypes.ts`, and nearby files for the operation or shape. Two slightly-different versions of the same thing is the worst outcome — worse than either version alone.

**The data model outlives the feature.** If the data shape is wrong, every feature built on it inherits the wrongness — so contracts (identifiers, nullability, required-vs-optional, ownership) get decided deliberately, not by accident of the first implementation. For any schema or contract change, trace what happens to *existing* data: orphaned rows, half-migrated states, rows created by the other app. The clean-new-data path is easy; messy-existing-data is where bugs live.

**Separate pure logic from I/O from platform.** Pure transforms are testable and reusable across apps (this is why shared logic lives in `packages/database/src/lib`); I/O wrappers hold integration concerns; platform-specific branching (`"Roam"`/`"Obsidian"`) is passed in as input, never hard-coded inside generic functions.

**Scope is a contract.** A PR titled X contains X — every hunk maps to the ticket. Out-of-scope discoveries become Linear tickets or TODOs with context (`// TODO(ENG-XXXX): … because …`), not opportunistic edits. Shared refactors that stacked PRs depend on go in their own base PR. Deferrals are stated in the PR, not left for the reviewer to discover.

**Prove it works by driving it.** Green unit tests don't demonstrate UI flows, multi-user behavior, or load-order effects. User-facing changes get a runtime demo (Loom) exercising the real flow; controls must initialize from persisted state, not just react to clicks. (The `/demo-handoff` skill covers how to demo stacked/parallel work.)

**Cross-app alignment beats local invention.** Roam↔Obsidian features share contracts. Before designing a Roam-side shape or UX, check how Obsidian already does it; match it or explicitly flag the divergence to the feature owner. "We found it easier in Obsidian to…" is a recurring, and usually correct, review response.

---

## Hard-learned lessons (with sources)

### Frontend (Roam plugin, website)

- **Tailwind on the predefined scale only.** No inline CSS, no arbitrary values (`h-[37px]`, `text-[15px]`), no hardcoded colors, no component-local `styles.css`. Why: consistent definitions are the point of Tailwind; arbitrary values fork the design system silently. Arbitrary values only when load-bearing (e.g. Radix CSS vars). (PR #958 and 6 others)
- **Hoist repeated/typo-prone string literals to named constants.** Selectors, prop keys, attribute names: define once, reference everywhere. Why: `"setting"` vs `"settings"` typos fail silently at runtime. (PR #1067 and 5 others)
- **Use current Roam APIs:** `ui.react.Block` to render blocks; `data.async.fast.q` / `data.async.q` for reads. Never sync `.q`; avoid `async.backend` (flaky). Why: sync/legacy paths block the main thread or intermittently fail. (4 PRs)
- **Settings persist to Roam block props** (the canonical store) and must preserve the `isNewSettingsStoreEnabled` gate/migration state the old accessors enforced. Bypassing an accessor silently forks the store. (4 PRs)
- **Names state exactly what they hold or do.** `setSearchTerm`, not `setSearch`; `initialLoad`, not `loaded`; UI labels specific enough that a user knows what happens. Why: a name the reader guesses wrong about is a bug vector. (PR #1214 and 6 others)
- **Domain vocabulary is reserved.** "Candidate" means *Candidate Nodes* in DG (likely a future DB concept) — don't use it for anything else in types/variables/functions. Before naming a cross-app concept, check what the sibling app already calls it and prefer that name (Obsidian's `publishedNodes` beat Roam-side `candidates`). Why: a name that collides with a domain term will be renamed in review; a name that diverges from the sibling app doubles the vocabulary. (PR #1216)
- **Type assertions are a last resort.** No `as`, `any`, `unknown`-and-cast for external APIs; narrow with type guards or fix the type at its source (add missing types to roamjs-components rather than casting around them). Same for `!`: "Avoid `!` whenever possible. If not possible, add a comment explaining why" (mdroidian, PRs #1329/#1324). For untyped third-party surfaces, maintain our own minimal `unofficial-types.ts` with only the types we need — don't add unofficial community typings packages to package.json (PR #1271). Why: assertions turn compile-time errors into runtime surprises. (6 PRs)
- **New UI is feature-gated.** If the parent feature has a flag, the new element checks it. "If we merge this, is it ready for Pilot Users?" must have an answer.
- **Prefer platform-native APIs: `window.roamAlphaAPI` > roamjs-components > hand-rolled.** The typed surface is not the full runtime surface — roamjs-components' types lag Roam's actual API (e.g. `data.page.fromMarkdown` / `data.block.fromMarkdown` exist but are untyped; declare locally and cast). Before concluding a capability doesn't exist, check `roam-api-surface.md` in this directory (regenerate per its instructions). Why: two independent ENG-1858 implementations diverged on exactly this — one hand-rolled a markdown parser the platform already ships. (ENG-1858, 2026-07; preference order set by sid.)
- **Helpers wrapping a `roamAlphaAPI` write must surface the promise.** A success-reporting path that fires-and-forgets a write claims success it can't know; a floating promise inside a shared helper (`setBlockProps` pre-ENG-1858) makes every caller unable to await. Fix the helper (return the promise), `void` the call sites that genuinely don't care. (ENG-1858)
- **New comments are load-bearing or absent.** A comment that restates the code or narrates the change is noise — mdroidian's literal words, twice: "Claude, chill on the comments" (PRs #1222, #1321; also #1292, #1284). A comment must be parseable by a cold reader from the file alone; one that references off-file context draws "What is F12?" / "What is the same reason?" instead of understanding. Why: agents over-comment by default, and every unclear comment is a review round-trip.
- **Persisted data stores stable IDs, never display names.** Names ("frameName") are subject to change and belong only in the UI at choosing time; saved data references by stable id (`frameShapeId`, uid). Why: name-keyed lookups silently break on rename. (PR #1222)
- **Look up settings-tree children by key, never by position.** `tree[3]` compiles, matches the tree you just built, and writes markdown into the wrong parent the moment someone reorders a setting; use `getSubTree({ tree, key: "Template" })`. (PR #1302)
- **`Page`, `Block`, and `Any` are reserved built-in vocabulary.** Excluded from user-selectable type lists (PR #1298, #1272); a remote schema is never resolved to a built-in solely by name, and a configured type never takes a reserved name — mapping a remote "Block" schema to the local built-in silently discards its identity, format, and semantics. #1331 was blocked on exactly this. For v0, block the names and ticket proper conflict resolution.
- **User-facing copy speaks user vocabulary; internal operations are silent.** A toast saying "backfilled" means nothing to a user — internal bookkeeping (backfills, migrations, sync housekeeping) reports to PostHog only. The toast rule from #1214 cuts both ways: user-affecting failures get a toast; internal milestones don't. (PR #1332)
- **A panel that replaces or extends existing UI matches it pixel-wise.** Proportions, selected-tab highlight, centering, spacing — reviewers screenshot-compare against the original and file each delta ("the styling menu is now stretched", "missing the purple highlight"). The canvas already had a Convert To submenu, gated to a single `text` or `image` shape. This widens the gate to `geo` and `note`, and routes all three call sites through one helper so the right-click menu and the `?C` dialog cannot drift apart.

Stacked on #1427 (ENG-1356), which extracted `replaceShapeWithDiscourseNode`. **#1427 must merge first.** Base is that branch, so this diff is only what ENG-1884 adds.

## Reviewer brief

- **Result**: right-clicking a sticky note or a rectangle with text offers Convert To, prefilled with the shape's text. Empty ones do not. `text` and `image` behave as before.
- **Review focus**: `apps/roam/src/components/canvas/convertShapeToDiscourseNode.ts`. `getConvertibleShapeText` returns the dialog's initial text, or `null` when the shape cannot convert; every gate is now `!== null` on that one value, replacing the `isTextSelected || isImageSelected` booleans that lived in two files. The positioning block in `replaceShapeWithDiscourseNode` is the riskiest part, see below.
- **Risk**: no live-graph run. See Verification.

## Decisions worth challenging

- **Empty geo and note shapes are excluded.** FEE-824 asks for conversion "if it has text in it", and offering Convert To on every blank rectangle adds a submenu to the common case. Empty `text` shapes stay convertible, which is today's behavior, so this is not a regression for them. The asymmetry is deliberate.
- **Arrows are excluded** even though `TLArrowShapeProps` carries `text`. Arrows already convert to relations through the adjacent Relation submenu, and offering both on one shape invites picking the wrong one. ENG-1892 covers the Obsidian side; no ticket covers arrow labels.
- **`isImageSelected` survives in both files.** It no longer gates the submenu, but it still filters `page-node` out of the type list, which is about images lacking a key-image flag rather than about convertibility.
- **`"text" in shape.props` rather than a cast.** It narrows the props union, so `shape.props.text` types as `string` with no `as` and no optional chaining. Same idiom as `defaultHandleExternalTextContent.ts:79`. The preceding `TEXT_SHAPE_TYPES` check is the policy allow-list, not a redundant guard: it is what keeps arrows out.
- **Positioning changed in `replaceShapeWithDiscourseNode`, which is base-PR code.** It created the node with no `parentId`, and tldraw reads `x`/`y` as page coordinates when no parent is given (`Editor.createShapes`). A shape's `x`/`y` are parent-relative, so converting a shape inside a frame placed the node at the wrong point and re-parented it by hit test. Passing `parentId` alone is not enough: deleting one child of a two-shape group makes `GroupShapeUtil.onChildrenChange` dissolve the group, so the captured `parentId` stops resolving. The code now captures the page point before the delete and positions by it whenever the parent did not survive. Pre-existing for `text` and `image`, but `geo` and `note` are far likelier to sit in a frame or a group, which is why it is fixed here rather than deferred.

`replaceShapeWithDiscourseNode` deletes the source shape and creates a new one, so arrows bound to a converted shape unbind and dangle. Pre-existing for `text` and `image`, more reachable now. Not fixed here.

The delete and the create are separate history entries, also pre-existing, so undoing a conversion takes two presses.

**Trimmed text** — I was passing `.trim()` to the dialog, so converting a deliberately indented text shape would silently rewrite its content. Trim now only decides whether a `geo`/`note` counts as empty; the dialog gets `props.text` unchanged.

- `getConvertibleShapeText` returns `""` for images, an overloaded falsy sentinel. All three callers correctly use `!== null`; splitting it into a predicate plus a getter adds more surface than it removes. Worth your call.
